title: The E1s63 doubling conjecture for minimally 3-rigid graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a minimally 3-rigid graph, and let $G'$ be obtained from $G$ by a 1-extension of type E1s63. Let $\mathbf{c}_{3}(G)$ denote the three-dimensional realization count. **The E1s63 doubling conjecture.** Then

$$
\frac{\mathbf{c}_{3}(G')}{\mathbf{c}_{3}(G)}=2.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by experiments in which E1s63 extensions always doubled the number of realizations. The supplied text does not establish the claim for all minimally 3-rigid graphs.
source_name: Georg Grasegger, “Explorations on the number of realizations of minimally rigid graphs”, arXiv:2502.04736 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04736

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).
